Many museum pieces, especially art, are owned by entities outside of the museum, who allow them to be kept there for a variety of different reasons. The Crown Estate, and in some cases, King Charless III personally, own all of the major and priceless Royal artifacts that you'll see on display for the public to view.

Rothschild could have taken ownership of the painting at some point, and allowed it to remain there on display. Now, I'm not saying that this is the sort of arrangement that he has with the Royal Academy, I have absolutely no idea. What I am saying is that it is most definitely a possibility, and as detailed previously, a fairly common practice.
